title: NIST O-RAN Security Testbed and Accepted Standards Contributions
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: NIST's project page records an active 5G Open Testbed, open-source automation software, and multiple 2025 change requests accepted into O-RAN test and security specifications.
key_findings: The project evaluates emerging O-RAN security requirements and testing processes for U.S. government use.
Laboratory work uses multiple open-source 5G RAN and core implementations.
Several NIST change requests were accepted or incorporated into O-RAN specification artifacts.
why_it_matters: The page connects federal wireless policy to laboratory infrastructure, software, and standards contributions rather than treating 6G as a single future promise.
ftfn_relevance: Defines later gates for reproducible tests, conformance, certification, interoperability, and deployment.
evidence_limits: The artifacts do not constitute a completed 6G standard or commercial network.
Accepted contributions do not prove broad multi-vendor interoperability, certification, or secure field deployment.
